newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Sweden trade surplus seen higher in March.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Sweden trade surplus seen higher in March.

text.p: Sweden's trade balance in March was expected to show a surplus of 11.4 billion crowns, a Reuters poll issued on Friday showed.
Forecasts from 10 analysts ranged between 9.8 billion and 12.5 billion crowns.
For calendar 1997, the trade balance was expected to be a 129.4 billion crown surplus, according to a survey of nine analysts. Forecasts varied between 115 and 140 billion crowns.
In February this year, Sweden had a trade surplus of 10.7 billion crowns. In March 1996, Sweden recorded a trade surplus of 11.4 billion crowns.
For full year 1996, there was a surplus of 94 billion crowns, according to Statistics Sweden.
Statistics Sweden will publish trade figures for March at 0800 GMT on April 25.
Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Carnegie, Consensus, Den Danske Bank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, JP Morgan, Nomura, PaineWebber, and Unibank.
Monthly figures only were provided by Nomura.
